title: Dale, trucker

greeting.text: The bell over the door. A big man in a work shirt, rubbing his eyes with the heel of his hand.
Evening. Large flat white, and whatever diesel you'll let me have. Can't see my own bonnet out there.

annoyed: Mate. I've shown you my hands. I've stood here like a stunned mullet. Coffee. Please.

notes.wrist: He taps his card and waits. Grease under the nails. The veins are where veins go.
notes.reflection: The mirror in the corner shows the whole shop, bent. Him from behind. You and Wren at the counter.
notes.shadow: You lean over the counter and look at the floor. He watches you do it.

topics.answer: Frozen peas to Mullane Flat. Should've been there by midnight. Then that muck came down off the tops and I've done the last ten k in second gear.
Bloke on forty kept saying he could see his wife on the roadside, waving him over. She passed six years back. I turned it off after that.

topics.ask: You look wrecked. Coffee's on the house.
topics.note: He means it. Beside you, Wren has gone very quiet.

topics.ask: How do I know you're really Dale?
topics.answer: Because it says so on my licence, my truck, and every letter from my ex-wife's solicitor. What sort of a question is that?

wren.arrive: First one of the night. Be nice. Not too nice.
wren.adviceLine: He's fine. Smell that? Diesel and servo coffee. Nothing out there copies that. Serve him and send him on.

serve.text: Cheers. Keep that door locked between customers, yeah? I mean it.
The bell again. His tail-lights are gone before he is out of second gear.

turnAway.text: The sign says open. There's eighty k of nothing out there, mate.

shelter.text: Road's no good tonight. There's a room out the back.
...Yeah. Yeah, alright. Wouldn't say no to four hours.

walkout.text: You know what, forget it. I'll take my chances with the fog.
He leaves the receipt curling on the counter.

report.serve: A B-double carrying frozen goods reached the Mullane Flat depot at ten past one. The driver told staff, quote, the kid on nights at Corrigan's looks like they haven't slept in a month. End quote.
report.turnAway: A B-double has been found jackknifed across both lanes eleven kilometres west of Corrigan's Pass. Engine running. Driver's door open. The driver has not been located.
report.walkout: A B-double has been found nose-down in the drain west of the pass. The cab was empty. There was a coffee cup on the dash, still full.
report.shelter: A truck driver who sat out the night at Corrigan's Roadhouse has checked in with his depot and is continuing west.
report.missed: A truck was seen idling at Corrigan's pumps a little before dawn. Nobody came out to it. It has since moved on.
